classification.difficultyReason: Translate the 95% exceedance requirement into a lower-tail cutoff, convert the quantile to a weight and round down to satisfy the whole-gram maximum.

content.prompt: A machine fills cereal boxes with weights that are normally distributed with mean 500 g and standard deviation 2 g. To ensure boxes are above the advertised weight at least 95% of the time, what is the greatest whole-gram weight that should be printed on the box?

answer.worked:
Let $w$ be the advertised weight. We require $P(X>w)\geq0.95$, so $P(X\leq w)\leq0.05$.

From the table, $P(Z\leq1.6)=0.9452$ and $P(Z\leq1.7)=0.9554$. Using the midpoint estimate and symmetry gives $z\approx-1.65$ for the lower 5% cutoff.

$$\begin{aligned}w&\approx500+(-1.65)(2)\\w&\approx496.7\text{ g}\end{aligned}$$

The greatest whole-gram advertised weight below this cutoff is **496 g**. Checking this choice:

$$\begin{aligned}z&=\frac{496-500}{2}\\z&=-2\\P(X>496)&=P(Z<2)\\P(X>496)&=0.9772\end{aligned}$$

Thus about 97.72% of boxes exceed the advertised weight, satisfying the requirement.
